import ctypes
import numpy as np

def assert_test():
    # Load the libraries
    ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgslcblas.so", mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
    gsl = ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgsl.so")

    # Define the function signature for gsl_sort_smallest_index
    gsl.gsl_sort_smallest_index.argtypes = [ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_size_t), ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_double), ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.c_size_t]
    gsl.gsl_sort_smallest_index.restype = ctypes.c_int

    def find_k_smallest_indices(k, array):
        n = len(array)
        if k > n:
            raise ValueError("k cannot be greater than the length of the array")

        # Convert Python list to ctypes array
        src = (ctypes.c_double * n)(*array)
        p = (ctypes.c_size_t * k)()

        # Call the C function
        result = gsl.gsl_sort_smallest_index(p, k, src, 1, n)
        if result != 0:
            raise RuntimeError("Error occurred in gsl_sort_smallest_index")

        # Convert ctypes array to Python list
        return list(p)

    # Test cases
    array = [3.1, 1.4, 2.7, 0.5, 4.8]

    # Test 1: Find 2 smallest indices
    indices = find_k_smallest_indices(2, array)
    assert indices == [3, 1], f"Expected [3, 1], got {indices}"

    # Test 2: Find 3 smallest indices
    indices = find_k_smallest_indices(3, array)
    assert indices == [3, 1, 2], f"Expected [3, 1, 2], got {indices}"

    # Test 3: Edge case with k = 0
    indices = find_k_smallest_indices(0, array)
    assert indices == [], f"Expected [], got {indices}"

    # Test 4: Edge case with k = len(array)
    indices = find_k_smallest_indices(len(array), array)
    assert indices == [3, 1, 2, 0, 4], f"Expected [3, 1, 2, 0, 4], got {indices}"

    # Test 5: Error case with k > len(array)
    try:
        find_k_smallest_indices(len(array) + 1, array)
    except ValueError as e:
        assert str(e) == "k cannot be greater than the length of the array", f"Unexpected error message: {str(e)}"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert_test()
